title: UP BOARD CLASS 11 — Biology | Biological Classification Five Kingdoms
description: Subject-wise test on Biological Classification Five Kingdoms (Biology) for UP BOARD CLASS 11. 50Q.
subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: The Five Kingdom Classification system was proposed by:

options.explanation: Carl Linnaeus is known for the two-kingdom system of classification.
Ernst Haeckel introduced the kingdom Protista.
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system in 1969.
Herbert Copeland proposed a four-kingdom system of classification.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system in 1969, categorizing organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following kingdoms primarily consists of unicellular prokaryotic organisms?

options.explanation: Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms.
Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.
Fungi consists of eukaryotic organisms.
Plantae consists of eukaryotic organisms.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera is characterized by the presence of prokaryotic organisms, which are typically unicellular and lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: The cell wall of fungi is chemically composed of which of the following substances?

options.explanation: Cellulose is found in plant cell walls.
Chitin is the primary component of fungal cell walls.
Peptidoglycan is found in bacterial cell walls.
Lignin is found in plant cell walls.

questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are unique in their composition, primarily made of chitin, a complex polysaccharide.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Amoeba and Paramecium are examples of organisms classified under which kingdom?

options.explanation: Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.
Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms that do not fit into other kingdoms.
Fungi consists of eukaryotic organisms with chitin cell walls.
Animalia consists of multicellular eukaryotic organisms.

questions.explanation: Amoeba and Paramecium are unicellular eukaryotes that do not fit into the categories of plants, animals, or fungi, and are therefore classified under Kingdom Protista.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion used by R.H. Whittaker for the Five Kingdom Classification?

options.explanation: Cell structure is a criterion used by R.H. Whittaker.
Thallus organization is a criterion used by R.H. Whittaker.
Mode of nutrition is a criterion used by R.H. Whittaker.
Presence of locomotory organs is not a primary criterion used by R.H. Whittaker.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker's main criteria for classification were cell structure, thallus organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: An organism is observed to be heterotrophic, eukaryotic, multicellular, and lacks a cell wall. To which kingdom would it most likely belong?

options.explanation: Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.
Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms that do not fit into other kingdoms.
Fungi consists of eukaryotic organisms with chitin cell walls.
Animalia consists of multicellular eukaryotic organisms that lack cell walls.

questions.explanation: The description matches the defining characteristics of organisms belonging to Kingdom Animalia.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding the members of Kingdom Protista?

options.explanation: Protista includes both photosynthetic and heterotrophic organisms.
Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms.

options.text: They represent a diverse group of unicellular eukaryotes.
options.explanation: Protista is a diverse group of unicellular eukaryotes.

options.text: They always possess a cell wall made of cellulose.
options.explanation: Not all Protista have a cell wall, and those that do may have cell walls made of different materials.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Protista is known for its diversity, encompassing unicellular eukaryotes that can be photosynthetic, heterotrophic, or mixotrophic.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Consider an organism that is eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, and reproduces primarily by spores. It plays a significant role in decomposition. This organism most likely belongs to which kingdom?

options.explanation: Plantae consists of autotrophic organisms.
Fungi consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that reproduce by spores.
Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms that do not fit into other kingdoms.
Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.

questions.explanation: The characteristics match the defining features of organisms belonging to Kingdom Fungi.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): All organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera are prokaryotic. Reason (R): Monerans lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is a correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true and explains the assertion.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true and is explained by the reason.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because the defining characteristic of Kingdom Monera is that its members are prokaryotic.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A newly discovered organism exhibits the following features: eukaryotic cell structure, presence of chloroplasts for photosynthesis, multicellular organization, and a life cycle that involves alternation of generations. Based on these features, it would be classified under which kingdom?

options.explanation: Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.
Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms that do not fit into other kingdoms.
Plantae consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, photosynthetic organisms with alternation of generations.
Fungi consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that reproduce by spores.

questions.explanation: The description matches the defining characteristics of organisms belonging to Kingdom Plantae.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: The five-kingdom classification system was proposed by

options.explanation: Carl Woese is known for his work on the three-domain system.
Ernst Haeckel proposed the kingdom Protista.
R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
A.V. Leeuwenhoek is known as the father of microbiology.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker proposed the widely accepted five-kingdom classification system in 1969, categorizing organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera

options.explanation: Eukaryotic cell structure is characteristic of other kingdoms.
Multicellular body organization is not a defining characteristic of Monera.
Presence of a true nucleus is characteristic of eukaryotic cells.
Prokaryotic cell structure is a defining characteristic of Monera.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera exclusively includes all prokaryotic organisms, which lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: The primary component of the cell wall in most fungi is

options.explanation: Cellulose is found in plant cell walls.
Peptidoglycan is characteristic of eubacterial cell walls.
Chitin is the primary component of the cell wall in most fungi.
Lignin is found in plant cell walls.

questions.explanation: Fungi possess a rigid cell wall primarily composed of chitin, a complex polysaccharide.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which group of organisms is commonly known as 'golden algae' and includes diatoms and desmids

options.explanation: Dinoflagellates are a different group of organisms.
Euglenoids are a different group of organisms.
Chrysophytes are commonly known as 'golden algae'.
Slime moulds are a different group of organisms.

questions.explanation: Chrysophytes are a group within Kingdom Protista that includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids).
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Viruses are not included in Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification primarily because

options.text: They are obligate parasites and cannot reproduce independently
options.explanation: While true, this is not the primary reason for their exclusion.

options.text: They lack a proper cellular structure and are considered acellular
options.explanation: Viruses are acellular, which is the primary reason for their exclusion.

options.text: They have genetic material that can be either DNA or RNA
options.explanation: This characteristic is not the primary reason for their exclusion.

options.text: They cause diseases in plants and animals
options.explanation: This characteristic is not the primary reason for their exclusion.

questions.explanation: The five-kingdom classification is based on cellular organization among other criteria. Viruses are acellular, meaning they do not possess a true cellular structure.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Fungi is INCORRECT

options.text: Most fungi are heterotrophic, obtaining nutrients as saprophytes or parasites
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The body of multicellular fungi consists of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: Fungi have a cell wall made of chitin and polysaccharides
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: All fungi are multicellular and filamentous
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because not all fungi are multicellular and filamentous.

questions.explanation: While most fungi are multicellular and filamentous, there are exceptions. Yeast is a well-known example of a unicellular fungus.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic algae or cyanobacteria, where both organisms mutually benefit, is termed as

options.explanation: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between fungi and the roots of higher plants.
Lichens are symbiotic associations between fungi and photosynthetic algae or cyanobacteria.
Nitrogen fixation is a different process.
Saprophytism is a different mode of nutrition.

questions.explanation: Lichens are classic examples of symbiotic associations between a fungal partner and an algal or cyanobacterial partner.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: An organism is observed to be unicellular, eukaryotic, and possesses flagella for locomotion. It has chloroplasts and performs photosynthesis in the presence of light, but can also switch to a heterotrophic mode of nutrition by engulfing food particles in the absence of light. This organism most likely belongs to which group

options.explanation: Dinoflagellates are a different group of organisms.
Euglenoids match the description provided.
Amoeboid protozoans are a different group of organisms.
Slime moulds are a different group of organisms.

questions.explanation: The description of being unicellular, eukaryotic, flagellated, and exhibiting both photosynthetic and heterotrophic nutrition perfectly describes Euglenoids.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Who proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system?

options.explanation: Ernst Haeckel is known for coining the term ecology and proposing the Gastraea theory, but not the Five Kingdom Classification.
Carolus Linnaeus is known for his work on the two-kingdom system of classification: Plantae and Animalia.
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification in 1969.
A.P. de Candolle is known for his work on plant classification, but not the Five Kingdom Classification.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification in 1969, which includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia, based on criteria like cell structure, thallus organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera?

options.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists of prokaryotic cells, which lack a true nucleus.
Most Monerans are unicellular.
Kingdom Monera consists exclusively of prokaryotic organisms.
Monerans can be autotrophic or heterotrophic.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists exclusively of prokaryotic organisms, meaning their cells lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: The cell wall of fungi is primarily composed of:

options.explanation: Cellulose is the primary component of plant cell walls.
Peptidoglycan is found in bacterial cell walls.
Chitin is the primary component of fungal cell walls.
Hemicellulose is a component of plant cell walls, but not the primary component of fungal cell walls.

questions.explanation: The cell wall of most fungi is made up of chitin, a complex polysaccharide.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a member of Kingdom Protista?

options.explanation: Escherichia coli is a bacterium, belonging to Kingdom Monera.
Agaricus is a fungus, belonging to Kingdom Fungi.
Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryotic organism, belonging to Kingdom Protista.
Spirogyra is a green alga, belonging to Kingdom Plantae.

questions.explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryotic organism that belongs to Kingdom Protista.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A major distinguishing feature between Kingdom Monera and Kingdom Protista is:

options.explanation: Both Monera and Protista can have cell walls, but they are composed of different materials.
Both kingdoms include organisms with various modes of nutrition.
The primary distinction between Monera and Protista is the presence of a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles in eukaryotic cells.
Flagella are present in some organisms of both kingdoms.

questions.explanation: Monera comprises prokaryotic organisms, while Protista includes all unicellular eukaryotic organisms.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: An organism is observed to be unicellular, eukaryotic, and capable of both photosynthesis and heterotrophic nutrition (mixotrophic). To which kingdom would it most likely belong?

options.explanation: Monera are prokaryotic and do not fit the description of being eukaryotic.
Protista includes unicellular eukaryotes with diverse modes of nutrition, including mixotrophy.
Fungi are primarily heterotrophic and do not perform photosynthesis.
Plantae are multicellular and primarily autotrophic, not mixotrophic.

questions.explanation: The description fits organisms like Euglena, which are characteristic members of Kingdom Protista.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: In the Five Kingdom Classification, the primary role of decomposers in ecosystems is fulfilled by organisms from which two kingdoms?

options.explanation: While some Protista can act as decomposers, they are not the primary decomposers.
Protista are not the primary decomposers in ecosystems.
Bacteria and Fungi are the primary decomposers, breaking down dead organic matter.
Plantae and Animalia are not primarily decomposers; they are producers and consumers, respectively.

questions.explanation: Bacteria (Kingdom Monera) and Fungi (Kingdom Fungi) are the principal decomposers in ecosystems.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following sets of characteristics accurately describes organisms of Kingdom Plantae in the context of the Five Kingdom Classification?

options.text: Multicellular, eukaryotic, heterotrophic, cell wall present
options.explanation: Plantae are primarily autotrophic, not heterotrophic.

options.text: Unicellular, eukaryotic, autotrophic, cell wall present
options.explanation: Plantae are multicellular, not unicellular.

options.text: Multicellular, eukaryotic, autotrophic, cell wall made of cellulose
options.explanation: This option accurately describes the characteristics of Kingdom Plantae.

options.text: Multicellular, prokaryotic, autotrophic, cell wall present
options.explanation: Plantae are eukaryotic, not prokaryotic.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Plantae includes multicellular, eukaryotic organisms that are primarily autotrophic and possess a rigid cell wall predominantly made of cellulose.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): All organisms belonging to Kingdom Protista are unicellular and eukaryotic. Reason (R): Protists show diverse modes of nutrition including autotrophic, heterotrophic, and saprophytic.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason does not explain the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, but they are independent characteristics of Protista.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true; Protista are indeed unicellular and eukaryotic.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true statements about Kingdom Protista, but the reason does not explain why Protista are unicellular and eukaryotic.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A newly discovered organism possesses a naked RNA molecule as its genetic material and causes diseases in plants. It lacks a protein coat. Based on the Five Kingdom Classification, how would this organism be categorized?

options.explanation: Viroids are not cellular and do not fit into any kingdom.
Viroids are not eukaryotic cells; they are acellular.

options.text: Kingdom Fungi (due to its parasitic nature)
options.explanation: The organism's characteristics do not match those of fungi.

options.text: It would not be classified under any of the five kingdoms.
options.explanation: Viroids, being acellular, are not classified within the Five Kingdom system.

questions.explanation: The description refers to a viroid, which is not included in the Five Kingdom Classification because it lacks a cellular structure.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following groups of organisms are included in Whittaker's Five-Kingdom Classification System?

options.explanation: Correct. These are the five kingdoms in Whittaker's system.
Archaea and Bacteria are part of Monera, not separate kingdoms in Whittaker's system.
Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes are not kingdoms but broad classifications.
Viruses are not included in Whittaker's five-kingdom system.

questions.explanation: Whittaker's Five-Kingdom Classification System includes Monera (prokaryotes like bacteria and archaea), Protista (eukaryotic microorganisms), Fungi (heterotrophic eukaryotes), Plantae (autotrophic eukaryotes), and Animalia (heterotrophic multicellular eukaryotes).
questions.hint: Recall the five kingdoms proposed by Whittaker.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which kingdom in Whittaker's classification includes organisms that are primarily decomposers and have chitinous cell walls?

options.explanation: Plantae have cellulose cell walls and are autotrophic.
Animalia lack cell walls and are heterotrophic.
Fungi are decomposers with chitinous cell walls.
Protista are diverse and not primarily decomposers with chitinous walls.

questions.explanation: Fungi are primarily decomposers and possess chitinous cell walls, which distinguishes them from other kingdoms. Plantae have cellulose cell walls, Animalia lack cell walls, and Protista are diverse but not primarily decomposers with chitinous walls.
questions.hint: Think about organisms that break down dead organic matter.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A student observes a unicellular organism under a microscope and notes that it has a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles but lacks a cell wall. Based on Whittaker's classification, this organism most likely belongs to which kingdom?

options.explanation: Monera are prokaryotes and lack a nucleus.
Protista are unicellular eukaryotes without a cell wall.
Fungi have chitinous cell walls.
Animalia are multicellular and lack cell walls, but are not unicellular.

questions.explanation: Protista includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles but lack a cell wall. Monera are prokaryotes (no nucleus), Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, and Animalia are multicellular.
questions.hint: Consider the presence of a nucleus and absence of a cell wall.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are classified under the kingdom Monera. Reason (R): Blue-green algae are prokaryotic organisms lacking a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are prokaryotes and are correctly classified under Monera. The Reason (R) correctly explains the Assertion (A).
questions.hint: Evaluate the relationship between the assertion and reason.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of members of the kingdom Plantae?

options.explanation: Plants are autotrophic and perform photosynthesis.

options.text: Multicellularity and cell wall made of cellulose
options.explanation: Plants are multicellular with cellulose cell walls.

options.text: Ability to move from one place to another
options.explanation: Plants are sessile and cannot move.
Plants are autotrophic.

questions.explanation: Members of Plantae are autotrophic, multicellular, and have cellulose cell walls, but they lack the ability to move from one place to another, unlike animals.
questions.hint: Recall the defining features of Plantae.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A scientist discovers a new organism that is multicellular, heterotrophic, and lacks chlorophyll. The organism absorbs nutrients from dead organic matter. Based on these characteristics, the organism most likely belongs to which kingdom?

options.explanation: Plantae are autotrophic and have chlorophyll.
Animalia are heterotrophic but do not absorb nutrients from dead matter.
Fungi are decomposers that absorb nutrients from dead organic matter.
Protista are mostly unicellular.

questions.explanation: The organism described is multicellular, heterotrophic, lacks chlorophyll, and absorbs nutrients from dead organic matter, which are key characteristics of fungi.
questions.hint: Consider organisms that decompose dead organic matter.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following kingdoms includes organisms that can be both autotrophic and heterotrophic depending on environmental conditions?

options.explanation: Plantae are strictly autotrophic.
Animalia are strictly heterotrophic.
Protista can switch between autotrophic and heterotrophic modes.
Monera are mostly autotrophic or heterotrophic but not both in the same organism.

questions.explanation: Protista is a diverse kingdom that includes organisms like Euglena, which can be autotrophic (photosynthetic) in the presence of light and heterotrophic (ingesting food) in the absence of light.
questions.hint: Think about organisms that can switch between feeding modes.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A student collects a sample from a pond and observes the following under the microscope: Presence of a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Lack of a cell wall. Motile with the help of flagella. Based on these observations, the organism most likely belongs to which kingdom?

options.explanation: Monera are prokaryotes and lack a nucleus.
Protista are unicellular eukaryotes, often motile and lack cell walls.
Fungi have cell walls and are not typically motile.
Plantae have cell walls and are not motile.

questions.explanation: The presence of a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles indicates the organism is eukaryotic. The lack of a cell wall and motility with flagella are characteristic features of many protists.
questions.hint: Consider eukaryotic unicellular organisms with motility.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following kingdoms includes organisms that can fix atmospheric nitrogen?

options.explanation: Plants do not fix nitrogen; they rely on bacteria.
Animals cannot fix nitrogen.
Fungi do not fix nitrogen.
Certain bacteria in Monera fix atmospheric nitrogen.

questions.explanation: Certain bacteria (e.g., Rhizobium) in the kingdom Monera can fix atmospheric nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Other kingdoms do not include nitrogen-fixing organisms.
questions.hint: Recall which organisms are known for nitrogen fixation.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: A student argues that viruses should be included in Whittaker's Five-Kingdom Classification System as a separate kingdom. Which of the following is the best counter-argument to this claim?

options.text: Viruses are not considered living organisms by many scientists because they cannot reproduce or carry out metabolic activities on their own.
options.explanation: Viruses lack cellular structure and require a host to replicate, so they are not classified as living organisms.

options.text: Viruses have DNA or RNA but no cytoplasm.
options.explanation: This is a characteristic of viruses but not the best counter-argument.
Size is not a defining factor for classification in Whittaker's system.

options.text: Viruses can infect all living organisms.
options.explanation: This is a property of viruses but not a valid counter-argument.

questions.explanation: Viruses are not considered living organisms by many scientists because they lack cellular structure and cannot reproduce or carry out metabolic activities independently. They require a host to replicate, which is why they are not included in Whittaker's classification system.
questions.hint: Consider the definition of life and viral characteristics.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Who proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system?

options.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus proposed the Two Kingdom Classification system.
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system in 1969.
Ernst Haeckel proposed the Three Kingdom Classification system.
A.V. Leeuwenhoek was a pioneer in microscopy but did not propose the Five Kingdom system.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification system in 1969, which is widely accepted today.
questions.hint: The system divides living organisms into five kingdoms based on cellular organization and mode of nutrition.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: All prokaryotic organisms are grouped together under which kingdom?

options.explanation: Protista includes eukaryotic organisms like amoeba and paramecium.
Kingdom Monera includes all prokaryotic organisms like bacteria and archaea.
Fungi are eukaryotic organisms with chitinous cell walls.
Plantae includes multicellular photosynthetic organisms.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera exclusively includes all prokaryotic organisms, which lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
questions.hint: Prokaryotes are organisms without a defined nucleus.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of organisms belonging to Kingdom Fungi?

options.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic and do not perform photosynthesis.
Fungi lack chlorophyll as they are heterotrophic.
The cell wall of fungi is primarily composed of chitin.

options.text: Motile cells throughout their life cycle
options.explanation: Fungi are generally non-motile except for some spores or gametes.

questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic organisms with a rigid cell wall primarily composed of chitin, unlike plants (cellulose) or bacteria (peptidoglycan). They lack chlorophyll and are non-motile.
questions.hint: Fungi obtain nutrients by decomposing organic matter or absorbing nutrients from their surroundings.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an organism belonging to Kingdom Protista?

options.explanation: Nostoc is a cyanobacterium and belongs to Kingdom Monera.
Agaricus is a fungus and belongs to Kingdom Fungi.
Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryotic organism belonging to Kingdom Protista.
Spirogyra is an alga and belongs to Kingdom Plantae.

questions.explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryotic organism that belongs to Kingdom Protista. Nostoc is a cyanobacterium (Monera), Agaricus is a fungus, and Spirogyra is an alga (Plantae).
questions.hint: Protista includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms like amoeba, paramecium, and euglena.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: The primary feature that distinguishes organisms of Kingdom Protista from Kingdom Monera is the:

options.explanation: Both kingdoms can have varied modes of nutrition.
Cell wall composition varies within both kingdoms.
Protists are eukaryotic with a true nucleus, while Monera are prokaryotic without a true nucleus.
Habitat is not a distinguishing feature between these kingdoms.

questions.explanation: Monerans are prokaryotic, meaning they lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. Protists, on the other hand, are eukaryotic, possessing a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. This is the fundamental difference.
questions.hint: Prokaryotes lack a defined nucleus, while eukaryotes have a well-defined nucleus.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: An organism is observed to be multicellular, heterotrophic, with a cell wall made of chitin, and reproduces by spores. To which kingdom would it most likely belong?

options.explanation: Monera includes prokaryotic organisms like bacteria.
Protista includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms.
Fungi are multicellular (or unicellular like yeast), heterotrophic, have chitinous cell walls, and reproduce by spores.
Plantae includes photosynthetic organisms with cellulose cell walls.

questions.explanation: The combination of multicellularity (though some are unicellular like yeast), heterotrophic nutrition, a chitinous cell wall, and reproduction by spores are defining characteristics of Kingdom Fungi.
questions.hint: Fungi are heterotrophic organisms with chitinous cell walls and reproduce via spores.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

questions.question: Decomposers play a crucial role in nutrient cycling in ecosystems. Which two kingdoms primarily consist of organisms that act as decomposers?

options.explanation: Plantae are primarily photosynthetic and not decomposers.
Protista and Animalia do not primarily act as decomposers.
Fungi and Monera (bacteria) are the primary decomposers in ecosystems.
Plantae are not decomposers.

questions.explanation: Bacteria (Kingdom Monera) and Fungi (Kingdom Fungi) are the primary decomposers in most ecosystems, breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients.
questions.hint: Decomposers break down dead organic matter to recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.
questions.subject: upbo11-biology

options.explanation: Monera includes prokaryotic organisms without a distinct nucleus.

Plantae includes multicellular photosynthetic organisms.
Fungi are heterotrophic and lack chloroplasts.

questions.explanation: The organism is unicellular and eukaryotic (distinct nucleus), which rules out Monera (prokaryotic) and Plantae (multicellular). The presence of chloroplasts for photosynthesis rules out Fungi (heterotrophic). Therefore, it fits the description of a photosynthetic protist, such as Euglena.
questions.hint: The organism is unicellular, eukaryotic, photosynthetic, and motile.

questions.question: While R.H. Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification is widely accepted, certain organisms pose challenges due to their unique nature. Which of the following organisms is often considered an exception or a 'borderline case' in this classification system due to its acellular structure and obligate parasitic nature?

options.explanation: Paramecium is a unicellular eukaryotic organism belonging to Kingdom Protista.
Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera.
Yeast is a unicellular fungus belonging to Kingdom Fungi.
Viruses are acellular and obligate parasites, making their classification in the Five Kingdom system problematic.

questions.explanation: Viruses are acellular and lack the cellular machinery to sustain themselves independently. They only exhibit characteristics of life when inside a host cell, making their classification within a kingdom system based on cellular organization highly problematic. Paramecium (Protista), Cyanobacteria (Monera), and Yeast (Fungi) fit well into their respective kingdoms.
questions.hint: Viruses are not composed of cells and cannot reproduce or carry out metabolic activities independently.

questions.question: Which of the following kingdoms primarily consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that lack a cell wall?

options.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic but have a cell wall made of chitin.
Plantae are autotrophic and have a cell wall made of cellulose.
Animalia consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic organisms without a cell wall.
Protista are mostly unicellular and do not primarily consist of multicellular organisms.

questions.explanation: Animalia is characterized by eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that do not possess a cell wall. Fungi are heterotrophic but have a cell wall (chitin). Plantae are autotrophic and have a cell wall (cellulose). Protista are mostly unicellular.
questions.hint: Consider the presence or absence of a cell wall and mode of nutrition.

questions.question: An organism is observed to be eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, and its cell walls are composed of chitin. Based on these characteristics, this organism should be classified under which kingdom?

options.explanation: Plantae are autotrophic and have cell walls made of cellulose.
Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms, which lack a nucleus.
Protista are primarily unicellular and do not have chitin cell walls.
Fungi are eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, and have cell walls made of chitin.

questions.explanation: The characteristics provided (eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, with cell walls made of chitin) are the defining features of the Kingdom Fungi. Plantae are autotrophic with cellulose cell walls. Monera are prokaryotic. Protista are primarily unicellular and diverse, but chitin cell walls are not their defining feature.
questions.hint: Focus on the composition of the cell wall and mode of nutrition.
